description.narrative: This project seeks to raise awareness on the risks associated with lack of transparency and effective oversight in the oil trade business, particularly, focusing on how these risks play out, when oil traders do business with host states (like Nigeria) affected byconflict and fragility. h It has focused on ensuring female participation in extractive resources governance, making sure women participate in local governing structures such as Community Development Committees, where decisions on resource allocation and management are made with other gate keepers in the oil and gas host communities. Year 2 will be based on scaling up achievements of year 1,such as, the setting up of Bayelsa State Women Economic Inclusion Committee that was achieved in year Member-women-inclusion-committee/ that shall be consolidated, ground truthing relating to establishment of Host Communities Trust Funds (HCTFs) by some (IOCs) settlors and collaborating with Nigeria’s National Assembly Committees related to extractive justice in compelling IOCs to steer towards extractive justice. In this sense, interventions shall seek to close the institutionalised opacity that has characterised the operations of the generally complex extractive sector in Nigeria, which has affected women (negatively) for many decades. The net effect of this is for a sector that accounts for bulk of government revenues that were effectively walled off from the generality of Nigerians in the past. While the complexity remains, the opacity is gradually giving way. Reports of the Nigeria Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (NEITI) have helped in opening this strategic sector to civic groups, the media, parliamentarians, and citizens. Ongoing reforms in the sector are also helping in breaking down the sturdy wall of secrecy. Much still needs to be done for women economic inclusion and extractive accountability. Through this project’s year 2, actors will be abletomake informed contributions on optimal and prudent management of extractive resources. Without doubt, knowledge-driven engagements by all of society, especially, civil society groups, will be a critical success factor in the quest for the reversal of theresource curse in Nigeria .

participating-org.narrative:
The Niger Delta Budget Monitoring Group, NDEBUMOG is a regional non- governmental organization formed in 2005, and works in the areas of budget advocacy, transparency, accountability and anti-corruption in the Niger Delta and Nigeria in general. It has the mission to promote transparency and accountability in the public resource management through pro-poor budgeting and anti-corruption in theNiger Delta and democratic consolidation in Nigeria. Novib and NDEBUMOG started collaborating in 2011 to support small initiative of Deepening Expenditure Line Tracking of States and LGAs within the Niger Delta focusing on mobilizing citizens and building capacity for the expenditure tracking using participatory approaches.
Following the success of the DELT4SLOG1, as reported in the 2012 Narrative report and observed by the toolbox team in March 2013, Oxfam Novib decided to support the planned DELT4SLOG 2 to deepen the achieved outcomes of the project in 2012. The project aims to gather useful budget data for advocacy through desk review and field budget tracking of capital projects in the selected locations, strengthen the capacity of CSOs, NDEBUMOG staff, Journalists and community representatives on budget tracking, and established platforms of engagement in Rivers, Bayelsa and Delta States to hold governments accountable on its stewardship through dialogue with the Legislatures and other government representatives.
